paper.title: MoDeSuite: Robot Learning Task Suite for Benchmarking Mobile Manipulation with Deformable Objects

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Benchmark for mobile manipulation of deformable objects with an explicit simulation-to-real study.

sections_read.purpose: Identify benchmark gaps for deformable mobile manipulation.
Inspect environments, observations and eight tasks.
Record benchmark scope and transfer gap.

research_question: How well do standard RL and imitation methods handle mobile manipulation of deformable objects and transfer to hardware?
contributions: An eight-task deformable mobile-manipulation suite with multiple observation/action settings.

method.summary: MoDeSuite standardizes robot, deformable objects, observations and tasks, then evaluates state- and image-based policies in simulation and on a real robot.
assumptions: The benchmark's simulated deformable dynamics approximate the target hardware setting.

embodiments: mobile manipulator in simulation and hardware
study_context.sample_or_scale: Eight tasks; 10 physical curtain trials for each image-policy method.

evaluation.design: RL and imitation baselines are evaluated in simulation; selected state and image policies are deployed on the real robot.

findings.finding: Image policies that worked in simulation failed to complete the real curtain task, exposing a severe visual sim-to-real gap.
findings.scope: The physical curtain task and the two reported image-policy baselines.

author_stated.limitation: The benchmark exposes a substantial simulation-to-real visual-domain gap for deformable manipulation.

reader_inferred.boundary: Simulation success in deformable loco-manipulation is not reliable evidence of hardware competence.
reader_inferred.basis: Neither image policy completed the physical task despite simulation success.

transfer_boundary: Useful as a stress test for deformable-object interaction; physical transfer remains unresolved.

design_strengths: Reports a direct hardware transfer failure rather than only simulation scores.
design_risks: The real evaluation is concentrated on one task.
Baseline tuning may not represent the best modern visuomotor policies.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: Baselines share benchmark observations and tasks, but the real-world comparison is narrow.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Task completion is decisive for transfer; simulation reward alone is not.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Task and interface definitions are detailed.
critical_appraisal.external_validity: One hardware platform and one physical deformable-task transfer study.

evidence_cards.claim: On the real curtain task, neither image policy completed any of 10 trials; retrieval reached the curtain in 2/10, while behavior cloning did not reach it.
evidence_cards.relation: Shows that deformable mobile-manipulation simulation gains can collapse under visual sim-to-real shift.
evidence_cards.summary: The deployment paragraph contrasts simulation success with physical failure.
evidence_cards.source_context: While the policies are successful in simulation, neither is able to complete the task in the real world. Specifically, the retrieval-based method managed to approach and make contact with the curtain in 2 out of 10 trials, whereas the behavior cloning (BC) policy failed to even reach the curtain.

quantitative.value_or_direction: 0/10 completions for both; 2/10 contact for retrieval

verification.rationale: The paragraph explicitly states simulation success, zero physical completion and the 2-of-10 contact result.
